solution: $P(\{\omega_{4}\})=\dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{9}=\dfrac{1}{6}$, so the odds in favour are $\dfrac{1}{6}:\dfrac{5}{6}=1:5$
solution_full: Odds in favour of an event $E$ equal to $m:n$ means $P(E)=\dfrac{m}{m+n}$. Hence $P(\{\omega_{1},\omega_{3}\})=\dfrac{1}{2}$. By additivity over the disjoint elementary events, $a+b=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
If $b=1$, then $a=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $P(\{\omega_{1}\})<0$ (and $P(\{\omega_{4}\})=\dfrac{3}{2}>1$). This violates the axiom $P(E)\ge 0$, so this root is rejected.
If $b=\dfrac{1}{3}$, then $a=\dfrac{1}{6}$ and the probabilities are $\dfrac{1}{6},\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{1}{6}$, all non-negative with sum $1$. This is the assignment.
$P(\{\omega_{4}\})=\dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{9}=\dfrac{1}{6}$ and $P(\{\omega_{4}\}^{c})=\dfrac{5}{6}$, so the odds in favour of $\{\omega_{4}\}$ are $1:5$.
originality_note: New: a probability assignment with a quadratic term, where the odds condition and P(S) = 1 give two candidate assignments and the non-negativity axiom (not the algebra) rejects one of them (way 5: odds linked with the axioms). Closest known: 'odds in favour of A are 2:3, find P(A)' and assignments of probabilities to sample points checked for validity. Different because: the validity check is the step that selects the answer.
